a.1: Solomon offers sacrifices at Gibeon. His choice of wisdom which God gives him.
a.2: Solomon's embassy to Hiram, who sends him a skilful workman and timber.
a.3: The plan and ornaments of the temple: the cherubims, the veil, and the pillars.
a.4: The altar of brass, the molten sea upon twelve oxen, the ten loaves, the candlesticks and other vessels and ornaments of the temple.
a.5: The ark is brought with great solemnity into the temple: the temple is filled with the glory of God.
a.7: Fire from heaven consumes the sacrifices. The solemnity of the dedication of the temple. God signifies his having heard Solomon's prayer: yet so if he continue to serve him.
a.9: The queen of Sheba admires the wisdom of Solomon. His riches and glory. His death.
a.10: Rehoboam answers the people roughly: upon which ten tribes revolt.
a.11: Rehoboam's reign. His kingdom is strengthened.
a.12: Rehoboam for his sins is delivered up into the hands of the king of Egypt: who carries away all the treasures of the temple.
a.13: Abijah's reign: his victory over Jeroboam.
a.14: The reign of Asa: his victory over the Ethiopians.
a.15: The prophecy of Azariah. Asa's covenant with God. He deposes his mother.
a.16: Asa is reproved for seeking help from the Syrians: his last acts and death.
a.17: Jehoshaphat's reign: his care for the instruction of his people: his numerous forces.
a.18: Jehoshaphat accompanies Ahab in his expedition against Ramoth; where Ahab is slain, as Micaiah had foretold.
a.19: Jehoshaphat's charge to the judges and to the Levites.
a.20: The Ammonites, Moabites, and Syrians combine against Jehoshaphat: he seeks God's help by public prayer and fasting. A prophet foretells that God will fight for his people: the enemies destroy one another. Jehoshaphat with his men gathers the spoils. He reigns in peace, but his navy perishes, for his society with wicked Ahaziah.
a.21: Joram's wicked reign: his punishment and death.
a.22: The reign and death of Ahaziah. The tyranny of Athaliah.
a.23: Jehoiada the high priest causes Joash to be made king: Athaliah to be slain, and idolatry to be destroyed.
a.24: Joash reigns well all the days of Jehoiada: afterwards falls into idolatry and causes Zechariah to be slain. He is slain himself by his servants.
a.25: Amaziah' reign: he begins well, but ends ill: he is overthrown by Joash, and slain by his people.
a.26: Uzziah reigns prosperously, till he invades the priests' office, upon which he is struck with a leprosy.
a.28: The wicked and unhappy reign of Ahaz.
a.29: Hezekiah purifies the temple, and restores religion.
a.30: Hezekiah invites all Israel to celebrate the pasch; the solemnity is kept fourteen days.
a.31: Idolatry is abolished; and provisions made for the ministers.
a.32: Sennacherib invades Judah:  his army is destroyed by an angel.  Hezekiah recovers from his sickness:  his other acts.
a.33: Manasseh for his manifold wickedness is led captive to Babylon: he repents, and is restored to his kingdom, and destroys idolatry: his successor Amon is slain by his servants.
a.34: Josiah destroys idolatry, repairs the temple, and renews the covenant between God and the people.
a.35: Josiah celebrates a most solemn pasch. He is slain by the king of Egypt.
a.36: The reigns of Jehoahaz, Jehoiakim, Jehoiachin, and Zedekiah: the captivity of Babylon released at length by Cyrus.

13:2: Michaia... Alias Maacah. Her father had also two names, viz., Absalom, or Abishalom, and Uriel.
13:5: A covenant of salt... That is, a firm and perpetual covenant. See Num. 18.19.
16:1: Six and thirtieth year of his kingdom... That is, of the kingdom of Judah, taking the date of it from the beginning of the reign of Reboam.
18:19: Who shall deceive, etc... See the annotations, 3 Kings 22.
22:2: Forty-two, etc... Divers Greek Bibles read thirty-two, agreeably to 4 Kings 8.17.
23:5: To the sabbath... That is, to perform in your weeks the functions of your office, or the weekly watches.
28:19: For he had stripped it of help... That is, Ahaz stripped the kingdom of Judah of the divine assistance by his wickedness, and by his introducing idolatry.
30:3: The host of heaven... The sun, moon, and stars.
33:3: The host of heaven... The sun, moon, and stars.
36:9: Eight years old... He was associated by his father to the kingdom, when he was but eight years old; but after his father's death, when he reigned alone, he was eighteen years old. 4 Kings 24.8.
